Mathematics 
Marking Scheme 
Higher Level 
Q6 
Model Solution – 30 Marks 
Marking Notes 
(b) 
|∠𝐴𝐷𝐵| = 90° [angle in semi-circle] 
So |∠𝐴𝐵𝐷| = 45° [isosceles, and angles in a 𝛥 ] 
So |∠𝐴𝐶𝐷| = 45° [standing on the same arc] 
So |∠𝐴𝐷𝐶| = 180 −45 −40 = 95° 
OR 
|∠𝐴𝐷𝐵| = 90° [angle in semi-circle] 
So |∠𝐴𝐵𝐷| = 45° [isosceles, and angles in a 𝛥 ] 
So |∠𝐶𝐷𝐵| = |∠𝐵𝐴𝐶| = 5° 
So |∠𝐴𝐷𝐶| = 90 + 5 = 95° 
Scale 10D (0,3,5,8,10) 
Low Partial Credit 
• Work of merit, for example, 
indicates 90° or right angle or 
|𝐴𝐷| = |𝐷𝐵| 
Mid Partial Credit 
• Finds 45° angle(s) in triangle 
𝐴𝐷𝐵 
• Indicates two equal angles 
standing on same arc 
High Partial Credit 
• Indicates two equal angles 
standing on same arc, and 
indicates 90° or uses given 
isosceles triangle 
(c) 
Most of proof may be given as construction 
Join 𝑃 to 𝑂 to 𝑄. 
The angle at the centre ( |∠𝑃𝑂𝑄| ) must be twice 
|∠𝑃𝑅𝑄|, so must be > 180°. 
So, the point 𝑂 has to be outside the triangle 𝑃𝑄𝑅. 
OR 
Assume that 𝑂 is inside the triangle 𝑃𝑄𝑅. 
Then |∠𝑃𝑂𝑄| < 180°, 
where ∠𝑃𝑂𝑄 is the angle in the triangle 𝑃𝑂𝑄. 
But |∠𝑃𝑅𝑄| is half this angle, so |∠𝑃𝑅𝑄| < 90°, 
a contradiction. 
OR 
Assume that 𝑂 is inside the triangle 𝑃𝑄𝑅. 
Join 𝑃 to 𝑂 and continue until you hit the circle 𝑘, 
on the minor arc between 𝑅 and 𝑄. Label this 
point 𝑆. 
Then |∠𝑃𝑅𝑆| = 90°, as [𝑃𝑆] is a diameter. 
But |𝑃𝑅𝑆| > |∠𝑃𝑅𝑄|, a contradiction. 
OR 
The line through 𝑅 perpendicular to 𝑃𝑅 intersects 
𝑘 on the arc joining 𝑃 to 𝑄 that doesn’t contain 𝑅. 
Label this point 𝑇. Join 𝑇 to 𝑃. The centre is the 
midpoint of [𝑇𝑃], which is outside the triangle 
𝑃𝑄𝑅. 
Scale 5B (0, 2, 5) 
Note: if proof by contradiction is 
presented, assume that given first 
line has been used, even if not 
stated by candidate.
